intro_html: Com suon is Saigon street food royalty: lemongrass-marinated pork chops charred hard, served over rice with a fried egg and fresh cucumber and tomato. This is the big-appetite bowl of the library, 65 grams of protein and 950 calories for about $5.04.
cost_closing_html: About $5.04 a bowl for lemongrass pork chops with rice, egg, and vegetables. A Vietnamese restaurant charges $16 for com suon, and their chop is half the size of yours.
shop_smart: Pork chops are the headline at about $29.17 for 7 pounds. That is a serious protein haul, and chops routinely hit sale prices under $3.50 a pound, time the buy and this bowl gets even cheaper.
The marinade is built from bottles you buy once: fish sauce, soy, oyster sauce, and honey. Their combined cost against this batch is a few dollars off jars that last months.
Eggs and canned diced tomatoes round out the bowl for under $5 combined. The canned tomatoes skip the produce-aisle price roulette and taste fine chilled next to rich pork.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Whisk the marinade: lemongrass paste, garlic, fish sauce, soy sauce, oyster sauce, honey, brown sugar, half the vegetable oil, and the grated onion. Coat the pork chops and marinate at least 30 minutes, overnight is better.
Cook the rice per the package and set it aside.
Sear the chops in a ripping hot pan or grill them, a few at a time, letting the sugars char at the edges. Cook to 145F and rest 5 minutes before slicing.
Simmer the leftover marinade in the pan drippings for a few minutes at a full boil to make a safe, glossy drizzle sauce.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil, one per serving, leaving the yolks as soft or firm as your meal prep nerves allow.
Slice the cucumbers and drain the diced tomatoes for the fresh side.
Build bowls: rice, sliced pork, egg on top, cucumber and tomato beside, sauce and green onions over everything.
portion_html: Weigh the rice and sliced pork in the pot, subtract the empty pot weight you wrote down, and divide by 14, then add an egg and an even share of the vegetables to each container. Every bowl lands at about 950 calories with 65 grams of protein. This is the biggest bowl on the site, plan your day around it.

head.keywords: com suon, vietnamese pork chops, lemongrass pork, broken rice bowl, high protein meal prep, vietnamese meal prep
steps: Marinate pork chops in lemongrass paste, garlic, fish sauce, soy, oyster sauce, honey, and brown sugar for 30 minutes or more.
Cook the rice and set aside.
Sear or grill the chops hard to 145F, then rest and slice.
Boil the leftover marinade into a drizzle sauce and fry one egg per serving.
Assemble bowls with rice, pork, egg, cucumber, and tomato, then portion into 14 containers.
